candidate.answerReason: Equal perimeters make the triangle side twice the hexagon side. The triangle contains four congruent small equilateral triangles, while the hexagon contains six of the same size, giving area 6.

methods.label: Divide both shapes into matching triangles
methods.explanation:
Equal perimeters mean that each triangle side is twice a hexagon side: the same total length is divided among three equal sides instead of six. This suggests dividing both shapes into equilateral triangles of the hexagon's side length.

Connect the hexagon's center to its six vertices. The six central angles are each \(360^\circ\div6=60^\circ\). Each resulting triangle has two equal radii as sides, so it is isosceles with a \(60^\circ\) angle and therefore equilateral.

Now join the midpoints of the original triangle's sides. Each midpoint segment is parallel to the opposite side and half its length. This divides the original triangle into four congruent equilateral triangles, each with the same side length as one of the hexagon's six pieces. Equilateral triangles with the same side length are congruent, so all these pieces have equal area.

The original triangle has area \(4\), making each small triangle's area \(4\div4=1\). The hexagon therefore has area
\[
6\cdot1=\boxed{6},
\]
choice C.
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary dissection, midpoint segments, and congruent equilateral triangles without requiring an area formula or formal similarity scaling.
